_about: Per-sport render policy (spec 7.19 / 11.9). block_minutes drives card width; lane_policy alt_lane = overlapping games on one network stack into lanes (CFB), market_filter = the market decides which regional game is on the row; primary_line spread|moneyline. title is the header lockup; week_label true = 'WEEK N' from the fixture week. local_row_label is the rail text for a synthesized local row whose carrier is TBA. prime_window_start (D2) is the local ET 24-hour time at which this sport's prime viewing window opens. It is a POLICY, not a schedule: the window a given day uses is the EARLIEST prime_window_start among the sports that actually have a game that day, and its close is the last program end (kickoff + that sport's block_minutes) - derived in web/lib/primewindow.js, never stored. RENDERING CONTRACT v1.7 (2026-09-05): the five PROGRAM sports join this file, which is what register section 12 asked for - prime_window_start (D2) and the open_ended reconciliation land in ONE change so the file does not end up with two competing shapes. Each carries a `_source` naming where its numbers came from. Their `open_ended` here is the PER-SPORT DEFAULT; a program's own programs.open_ended column wins when it is set, which - the column being NOT NULL - is always, so this policy value is the fallback for a feed that omits the field. block_minutes is likewise a fallback: a program carries its own expected_duration_min, because a 360-minute fight card and a 120-minute wrestling show cannot share one number.

nascar.title: NASCAR
nascar._source: block_minutes = data/duration_defaults.json race_session.default. prime_window_start DERIVED: the earliest ET start among the 98 loaded 2026 races is 12:00 (OnlyBulls Green Flag 150 at St. Petersburg, Feb 28), read from the recorded cf.nascar.com fixtures through adapters/nascar.py. open_ended per duration_defaults race_session.open_ended_default - a caution moves the end.

indycar.title: INDYCAR
indycar._source: block_minutes from docs/research/indycar.md section 4 (~150 road/street). prime_window_start from the same doc section 2: the Indy 500 is a six-hour window from 10 AM, the earliest slot the season carries.

ufc.title: UFC
ufc._source: block_minutes = data/duration_defaults.json fight_card.default (one card, early prelims through main card). prime_window_start from docs/research/ufc.md section 1: the earliest main-card time on the Paramount+ schedule page is 2 PM ET (UFC 333 Abu Dhabi, Oct 24). primary_line per register section 9 - moneylines under show_odds; no provider is wired, so nothing renders yet.

wwe.title: WWE
wwe._source: block_minutes = data/duration_defaults.json weekly_show wwe-raw/wwe-smackdown (three hours). prime_window_start from docs/research/wwe.md section 5: PLEs are Saturday 6-10 PM ET, earlier than Raw's and SmackDown's 8 PM. Weekly shows have a fixed end (wwe.md section 4), so open_ended is false; a PLE row carries its own true, which is what the per-program column is for.

aew.title: AEW
aew._source: block_minutes = data/duration_defaults.json weekly_show aew-dynamite/collision. prime_window_start from docs/research/aew.md section 2: Collision: Tailgate to All Out is TNT Sat 7 PM ET, earlier than the 8 PM Dynamite/Collision slot.
